cards.explanation: The answer is True. The text says it flat out: "So King Solomon surpassed all the kings of the earth in riches and wisdom." (2 Chronicles 9:22) Solomon, David's son and Israel's king, wasn't just ahead of the pack. He was ahead of ALL the kings on earth. I'd need a lot more than a quarter to compete with that, friends.

The answer is to hear the wisdom God put in his heart. "All the kings of the earth sought an audience with Solomon to hear the wisdom that God had put in his heart." (2 Chronicles 9:23) Kings came from all over the earth just to listen. Picture a king showing up at the door for wisdom, bakers. I'd have shown up with a tray of cookies.
The answer is forty years. "Solomon reigned in Jerusalem over all Israel forty years." (2 Chronicles 9:30) Forty years is a long time to hold a throne, friends. That's a lot of mornings to be king.

The answer is David. "…Solomon rested with his fathers and was buried in the city of his father David." (2 Chronicles 9:31) David was Solomon's father, and Solomon reigned in David's place (1 Chronicles 29:23). All that gold, and the passage ends with a burial. That tells you something big, friends.
The answer is his son Rehoboam. "And his son Rehoboam reigned in his place." (2 Chronicles 9:31) Solomon's reign ends, and his son takes the throne. The passage closes on that handoff, friends.
